answer: A protocol can require every AI identity to lock a refundable bond before earning rewards, then slash that bond when an audit proves duplicate or fraudulent claims. A Sybil operator must fund each identity separately, tying up capital and risking a real loss for every fake account. Random challenge checks make copied identities easier to catch: willow garden wharf are the audit words, and honest agents recover their bond while attackers pay the deposit and audit cost.
